{{Short description|American physicist (1945–2020)}}
'''Harold Matthew Spinka Jr.''' (April 2, 1945, Chicago – December 27, 2020, [[Naperville, Illinois]])<ref name=obitHMSpinka>{{cite web|title=Harold Matthew "Hal" Spinka, Jr. April 2, 1945 - December 27, 2020|website=Friedrich-Jones Funeral Home, Naperville, Illinois|url=https://www.friedrichjones.com/obituaries/Harold-M-Hal-Spinka-Jr?obId=19433264}}</ref> was an American physicist, specializing in experimental [[particle physics]].<ref name=APSfellow>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2007&unit_id=&institution=Argonne+National+Laboratory}} (search on year=2007 and institution=Argonne National Library)</ref>

==Biography==
He graduated in 1966 with a bachelor's degree from [[Northwestern University]] and in 1970 with a Ph.D. in physics from [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech).<ref name=Marquis>{{cite web|title=Harold Matthew Spinka Jr., PhD, Presented with the Albert Nelson Marquis Lifetime Achievement Award|website=Marquis Who's Who|date=May 21, 2020|url=https://www.24-7pressrelease.com/press-release/472862/harold-matthew-spinka-jr-phd-presented-with-the-albert-nelson-marquis-lifetime-achievement-award-by-marquis-whos-who}}</ref> His doctoral dissertation ''The <sup>16</sup>O + <sup>16</sup>O reaction'' was supervised by Thomas Anthony Tombrello (1936–2014).<ref>{{cite thesis|title=''The <sup>16</sup>O + <sup>16</sup>O reaction'' by Harold Spinka|website=CaltechTHESIS, Caltech Library Service|date=September 24, 2014|doi=10.7907/XPJ4-A792 |url=https://thesis.library.caltech.edu/6186/ |last1=Spinka |first1=Harold |type=phd }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Obituary. Thomas A. Tombrello|website=Caltech News|date=24 September 2014 |url=https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/thomas-tombrello-43824}}</ref> From to 1970 to 1973 Spinka was a postdoctoral fellow at [[Argonne National Laboratory]]. In February 1973 he married Katherine Marie Wick (1950–2012).<ref name=obitKMSpinka>{{cite news|title=Obituary. Katherine Marie Spinka|newspaper=Daily Herald (Suburban Chicago's Information Source)|date=July 13, 2012|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/dailyherald/name/katherine-spinka-obituary?id=25334097}}</ref> From 1973 to 1976 he was an adjunct assistant professor at UCLA ([[University of California, Los Angeles]]).<ref name=Marquis/> His wife graduated from UCLA in 1976 with a Ph.D. in anatomy.<ref name=obitKMSpinka/>

After resigning from UCLA, he returned to Argonne National Laboratory, where he spent his career as a physicist, senior physicist, and research associate. One of his mentors and close friends was Akihiko Yokosawa (1927–2009).<ref name=Marquis/><ref>{{cite news|title=Dr. Akihiko 'Aki' Yokosawa, 1927-2009|author=Giangrasse, Joan|newspaper=Chicago Tribune|date=May 29, 2009|url=https://www.chicagotribune/news/ct-xpm-2009-05-29-090520114-story.html}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> From 1983 to 1986 Spinka was a member of the progressive advisory committee of the Los Alamos Meson Physics Facility (LAMPF), renamed in 1995 the [[Los Alamos Neutron Science Center]] (LANSCE). He is known for his research on [[w:Hexaquark|dibaryon resonance]]s, the [[Spin (physics)|spin]] structure of the [[proton]] studied using the [[Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider]] (RHIC) at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]], and the [[Dark Energy Survey]] (DES) relating to the identification of [[supernova]] candidates.<ref name=Marquis/> He also did important work involving the [[Zero Gradient Synchrotron]] (ZGS) and the [[Alternating Gradient Synchrotron]] (AGS).<ref name=APSfellow/>

In 2007 Spinka was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] for "his contributions to spin physics and leadership of symmetry experiments at ZGS, LAMPF, AGS, and RHIC."<ref name=APSfellow/>

He participated in competitive swimming until the age of 73. He enjoyed working with students and often served as a judge at science fairs. Upon his death he was survived by a daughter, a son, and five grandchildren.<ref name=obitHMSpinka/>
